paragraphs: Rav Kahana bar Taḥlifa, in Rav's name; see Ze'eira and Ḥanan bar Ba. 'He objected against Rav Kahana bar Mattityahu: R. Akiva holds liable,' etc., Menaḥot (66b). In שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas]: 'He objected against Kahana from what is taught: R. Akiva holds liable.' Thus the words 'bar Mattityahu' are a scribal error. In Kahana bar Minyomi's name. In Eruvin (8b): Rav Kahana bar Taḥlifa, in the name of Rav Kahana bar Minyomi, in the name of Rav Kahana bar Malkyo, in the name of Rav Kahana, Rav's teacher; some say Kahana bar Malkyo himself was Rav's teacher, etc. Rav Kahana said, 'Since this is Kahana's teaching, let me say something about it,' etc. Yuḥasin writes in the first chapter of Eruvin: Kahana bar Mattityahu, in Kahana bar Minyomi's name, etc. This is a scribal error, for the reading is as I transcribed. Only in Menaḥot there does our present reading have 'He objected against Kahana bar Mattityahu,' as above. I have already shown that it is a scribal error and should follow the aforementioned שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas]. She'erit Yosef lists Rav Kahana bar Mattana among Rav's students. I found no mention of him throughout the Shas; perhaps he means the aforementioned bar Mattityahu, but that is actually a scribal error. Nor have we found him speaking in Rav's name.
